title: AI Corrects Its Own Drawing Mistakes: SenseTime Open-Sources U1.6 Multimodal Model That Learns to Look Back
excerpt: The most common frustration with AI image generation is that text in the image comes out misspelled or the layout is skewed, and you still have to rework it man
content_html:
The most common frustration with AI image generation is that text in the image comes out misspelled or the layout is skewed, and you still have to rework it manually. On November 24, SenseTime released and open-sourced the SenseNova U1.6 native multimodal model. It continues the U series' paradigm of unified understanding and generation, and for the first time brings native image self-correction to the series' 8B open-source model.

Draw a draft first, then catch its own mistakes

After self-correction is enabled, the same model first generates a draft, then checks the image against the original prompt. If it finds text problems, it generates a corrected version—generation and error spotting are completed in a closed loop by one model. Detail refinement also covers portrait lighting, illustration brushwork, and the coordination of fonts and layout in posters. In text generation, U1.6 strengthens complex expressions such as perspective text and artistic typography, and introduces an infographic aesthetics model focused on text and layout. While improving accuracy, it preserves font expressiveness, spatial perspective, and layout aesthetics. A single image generation can produce a poster that combines text and visuals, and it can also handle unconventional glyphs and handwriting, turning "text" into a creative element in the image.
